title: NARUTO SHIPPUDEN: Ultimate Ninja STORM 4
provenance: verified locally on Apple Silicon (M1 Pro), engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2, macOS 26.6.2, Highball 0.9.3
notes: Installs and runs on DXMT. Tested 2026-09-10 on an M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r2: the opening movie and the title screen render correctly at 1920x1080 with DXMT 0.80 at D3D11 feature level 11_0, holding the game's own 30 fps cinematic cap with only 3 to 9 ms of GPU per frame, so there is a lot of headroom left. Game Mode was on and the game presented directly rather than through the compositor for part of the run. Before it will start, Steam shows a Bandai Namco end user licence agreement inside the Steam window that has to be accepted once: until it is, NSUNS4.exe starts and then sits at a few megabytes of memory forever with clean logs, which looks exactly like a hang (issue #74). Not yet measured in a battle: the menus need a controller or keyboard and the automation used for this run could not deliver key presses to the game, which is a limit of the test rig and not a fault of the game. Anyone playing normally with a keyboard or pad should get past the title screen.

dxmt.detail: opening movie and title screen at 1920x1080, the game's 30 fps cinematic cap with 3-9 ms GPU per frame, DXMT 0.80 D3D11 FL 11_0 (2026-09-10, r2, macOS 26.6.2, M1 Pro). A battle was not reached, see notes.

verified.fps: 30 at the title screen, which is the game's own cinematic cap, with 3-9 ms of GPU per frame
